verifications.claim: NASA is targeting April 1, 2026, for the launch of the Artemis II mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'Launch date NET April 1, 2026'; R5: 'maintaining the opportunity for a Wednesday, April 1, launch attempt'; R7: 'NASA has set April 1 as the target launch date'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state NASA targeting April 1, 2026, as the launch date or first window.

verifications.claim: Artemis II mission is a 10-day crewed mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'orbit the Moon on a 10-day mission'; R3: 'Mission duration 10 days (planned)'; R4: 'The 10-day flight'; R7: '10-day test flight'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly describe it as a 10-day crewed mission.

verifications.claim: Artemis II mission will fly around the moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'set off to orbit the Moon'; R3: 'crewed lunar flyby... free-return trajectory around the Moon'; R6: 'slingshot around it'
verifications.reasoning: Direct descriptions of lunar flyby or orbiting around the Moon.

verifications.claim: Artemis II mission marks the first human spaceflight to the lunar vicinity since 1972.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'For the first time since 1972'; R3: 'first crewed deep-space and lunar mission since Apollo 17 in 1972'; R6: 'first time humans have flown to the moon since December 1972'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state it as the first since 1972/Apollo 17.

verifications.claim: The rocket and spacecraft are scheduled to roll to the launch pad on March 19, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'would be rolled out the following day [March 19]'; R5: 'targeting 8 p.m. EDT on Thursday, March 19, to start rolling'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm it was scheduled/targeted for March 19, though later delayed to 20.

verifications.claim: Artemis II mission duration is approximately 10 days.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '10-day mission'; R3: '10 days (planned)'; R4: '10-day flight'
verifications.reasoning: Consistent description of 10-day duration across sources.

verifications.evidence: R1: 'first crewed flight of the SLS rocket and Orion spacecraft'; R3: 'first crewed mission of the Orion spacecraft'
verifications.reasoning: Direct statements confirming first crewed SLS/Orion flight.

verifications.claim: Artemis II mission was previously delayed from earlier in 2026, as reported by Spaceflight Now and Space.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'delayed both the earliest possible launch date... no earlier than Feb. 8'; R3: delays from Feb to March to April; R6: 'scrapped plans for launch dates in February and March'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm delays from earlier 2026 dates (Feb/March); R2 is Spaceflight Now.

verifications.claim: Artemis II mission was delayed due to technical issues including heat shield repairs and cold weather testing, as reported by Spaceflight Now and Space.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Abnormally cold weather forecast... delayed'; R3: 'no replacing the heat shield for Artemis II' (trajectory change instead); no 'heat shield repairs' or 'cold weather testing'
verifications.reasoning: Cold weather delayed (R2), but no heat shield repairs (R3: not replaced) or 'cold weather testing'; specifics contradict.
